title: precheck says which part of a check fails, and planning checks pool rows with bench_pool's own predicates
goal: backlog.py precheck prints, for a failing check, the last 20 lines of its output under the check's line, so a planner sees a check that fails for the wrong reason (SP-7y6dk257: ST-2p5ywkam's hand regex failed on one of six path-only rows and passed with four still path-only after the work); and the sprint planning rules ask a check over pool rows to call the code's own predicate (bench_pool.path_only, too_broad) rather than a new regex. Retrospective of SP-7y6dk257.

run: import re,subprocess,sys,tempfile;d=tempfile.mkdtemp();R=lambda*a:subprocess.run([sys.executable,'_tools/backlog.py','--root',d,*a],capture_output=True,text=True);subprocess.run(['git','init','-q',d],check=True);s=re.search(r'SP-\w{8}',R('new','sprint','--title','T','--goal','G').stdout).group(0);R('new','story','--title','P','--goal','G','--sprint',s,'--touch','x.txt','--check','python3 -c "import sys;print(1234567);sys.exit(1)"');p=R('precheck',s);ok='1234567' in p.stdout+p.stderr;print('precheck prints the output of a failing check:',ok);sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

import sys;t=open('.claude/skills/kb-sprint/SKILL.md',encoding='utf-8').read();p=t.split('## plan')[1].split('## start SP')[0];ok='bench_pool' in p and 'path_only' in p;print('plan step names the pool predicates:',ok);sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

gates.question: How much of a failing check's output does backlog.py precheck print: all of it, or its last lines?
options: last 20 lines of the check's stdout and stderr together, under the check's own line
gates.recommendation: last 20 lines of the check's stdout and stderr together, under the check's own line
gates.answer: last 20 lines of the check's stdout and stderr together, under the check's own line

notes: SP-yzgetyu2 close (2026-10-09), accepted by the operator: ST-s6tqojsw's planned call-count check failed at plan on ModuleNotFoundError (runpy.run_path puts no _tools on sys.path), and precheck counted it as failing before the work, so the premise proved nothing and the check was fixed mid-run; a check that fails on an exception or traceback at plan is a broken check, not a failing premise, and precheck says so. Planned at the 2026-10-10 whole-backlog triage, which the operator asked to end with every draft planned into a sprint or dropped (sprint 12 of 13, "Planning rules 2: plan-time warnings and probes"); it blocks no fitness test and no real user reported it, so it sits in a late sprint of the sequence. Premise: backlog.py precheck SP prints nothing for a failing check (the item's first check, which runs a throwaway sprint whose story's check prints 1234567 and exits 1). Run at plan 2026-10-10: exit 1, 1234567 is absent from precheck's output on the base, so the premise reproduces; the second check reads the plan section for bench_pool and path_only and fails on the base too. Selector: no test is named, so the check is a behavioural probe and a worker may add a test.
